resale_co.name: Certificate of Housing Code Compliance
resale_co.issued_by: City of Trenton Department of Inspections, Division of Housing Inspections
requirements: Home must conform to the City's existing Zoning and Fire Safety Codes
Smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm compliance (City Code Chapter 132, Section 40)
Must substantially meet the City's minimum habitability standards (Chapter 132, Articles V-VIII)
Electrical and plumbing service and fixtures must be safe, sound and sturdy and not create a fire, safety or life hazard

fees.label: Certificate of Housing Code Compliance (1 to 4 units)
fees.quote: The fee for a Certificate of Housing Code Compliance is $200.

fees.label: Each unit over four (structures with more than four units)
fees.quote: Structures with more than four units will pay an additional $15 per unit.

fees.label: Each re-inspection after the first (1 and 2 unit homes)
fees.quote: If more than one re-inspection is required a fee of $50 will be charged for 1 and 2 units.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply to the Division of Housing Inspections, Department of Inspections, City Hall Annex, 319 East State Street, 2nd Floor, Trenton, NJ 08608 (609-989-3550; Housing Inspections line 609-989-3563). No online application form was found; call the Division for the application. If the certificate cannot be obtained before closing, the owner may file an affidavit that the home will not be occupied until the certificate is issued. A Certificate of Approval or Certificate of Continued Occupancy is accepted instead.

evidence.quote: Prior to the change of ownership of any residential property a Certificate of Housing Code Compliance shall have first been obtained from the Department of Inspections, Division of Housing Inspections.

This document issued by the Director shall certify that the residential property conforms to the existing Zoning and Fire Safety Codes of the City of Trenton, Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Compliance as set forth in Chapter 132 Section 40

In lieu of the Certificate of Housing Code Compliance the change of ownership may occur if the owner files with the Department of Inspections an affidavit indicating that the property will not be occupied until such time as a Certificate of Housing Code Compliance is obtained.
A Certificate of Approval and/or Certificate of Continued Occupancy are acceptable substitutes for a Certificate of Housing Code Compliance.
All complaints regarding any violations may be given to the Division by calling 609-989-3563
Yolanda Vazquez Chief Housing Inspector Send Email Phone: 609-989-3542
319 East State Street 2nd Floor Annex Trenton , NJ 08608 Phone: 609-989-3550

resale_co.notes: Trenton's page quotes City Code sections 132-108 to 132-113 (Transfer of Property). The inspector's email yvazquez@trentonnj.org is taken from the 'Send Email' link on the official Inspections Department page (not shown as text). The Senior Housing Inspector is Leonard Martin, 609-989-3524 (City directory). The absentee owner (rental) license, vacant property registration and rental re-inspection fees are rental or vacancy programs, not sale requirements. The fee page is undated.

fire_cert.notes: The July 2026 LEA registry lists the State (S) as Trenton's fire code enforcing agency, but the state's list of State-enforced towns (July 17, 2026) shows Trenton without the 'SC' (smoke certificates) mark, and the state directory's smoke detector compliance block for Trenton is blank. The City's transfer-of-property rule makes smoke and CO compliance part of the Certificate of Housing Code Compliance, so the City housing division appears to be the issuer. Trenton Fire Department Fire Prevention is at 609-989-4032 (education only on its page). No information on extinguishers or the secondary power source label was found.

other_items.label: Zoning conformity
other_items.detail: The Certificate of Housing Code Compliance certifies the home conforms to the City's existing Zoning Code.

other_items.label: Affidavit option
other_items.detail: If the certificate is not ready, the sale may close if the owner files an affidavit that the property will not be occupied until the certificate is obtained.
